subtype: Approach: taking turns by the clock [Action]
passage: The two brothers, Harsha and Bhavesh, had one tablet between them and a fight every afternoon. "I've been playing for less time!" "No, you've had it for an hour!" Then Harsha had an idea. He fetched the kitchen timer from the shelf, a round white one that ticked. "Thirty minutes each. When it rings, the tablet moves." Bhavesh went first, watching the dial go round. When the bell rang he grumbled and handed it over. Harsha set the timer again. There was no argument about who had played longer, because the clock decided, and by evening their mother found them side by side, waiting for their turns.

qa.q: How long did each brother get with the tablet?
What was Harsha feeling when the fight about time kept happening?
qa.a: Harsha was probably frustrated and tired of arguing, which led him to look for a fairer way with the timer. 😠

qa.q: What alternative approach could the brothers use, and why?
qa.a: They could pick a two-player game they both enjoy, or agree on days for each of them. Either way the fight over minutes would be gone.

qa.q: How might Bhavesh see the timer?
qa.a: Bhavesh grumbled when the bell rang, so Bhavesh probably found it fair but also disappointing to give the tablet up on time.

grounding: Two brothers who share one tablet use a kitchen timer to give each thirty minutes, so the fixed time settles the argument about who played longer.
